newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. Sept T-bonds set seven-month high.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. Sept T-bonds set seven-month high.

text.p: U.S. debt futures continued to rise from Thursday's rally, with September T-bonds setting a fresh seven-month high at midsession, traders and technical analysts said.

September T-bonds inched up to 113-30/32, above resistance at 113-28/32. Major resistance rests at 114-00. Likewise, December Eurodollars expanded gains above the key 94.00 level and the 200-day moving average which is at 93.83, they said.
"This is really confounding those who were waiting to buy dips," said Dave Lundgren, senior technical analyst at Technical Data.

Many traders had expected both T-bonds and Eurodollars to succumb to profit-taking after September T-bonds rose to 113-15/32 during Thursday's shortened pre-holiday session in reaction to U.S. June labor data.
The payrolls report and unemployment rate suggested the U.S. labor sector was slackening after a robust first quarter.
Several technical analysts noted that sentiment had started to turn bullish on June 12 when U.S. May retail sales report was released. Sales fell 0.1 percent, the third monthly drop in a row.
"People believe we are in a narrow trading range, but a higher range," one Eurodollar futures analyst said.
December rose to 94.08, as it priced in no U.S. rate hike for the rest of the year, traders said.
Resistance for December Eurodollars is at 94.12, which represents a triple settlement high from mid- to late February, he said.

In September T-bonds, locals were caught short at 113-25/32 when the contract advanced through 113-28/32. After the opening both locals and dealers were forced to cover short positions once it tested 113-16/32.
Lundgren said September's rally to 113-16/32, a trendline from the contract's 1996 highs, represented a breakout from this year's sideways consolidative range.
He said the moving average/convergence divergence, a moving average derived from the difference between two moving averages, turned bullish in the daily, weekly and monthly timeframes.

The next major upside resistance is at 116-28/32, the second peak of the 1996 triangle on the monthly continuation chart. However, the contract would still remain locked in an even larger triangle that started in 1993.
The second peak of the 1993 triangle is at 122-04/32 on the monthly charts. ((Chicago derivatives desk (312)408-8750))
